question: Should OpenClaw add a native context-pressure alert and recovery contract for child/subagent sessions, and what should notify the parent or operator?
rationale: Current code exposes context usage data but has no product contract for thresholds, parent identity, notification targets, or recovery action, and VISION.md cautions against broad agent-hierarchy frameworks as a default architecture.

options.title: Define observe-first context-pressure alerts
options.body: Add a narrow diagnostic/session-health contract that alerts the parent/operator when a child crosses a chosen threshold, with recovery left explicit until live proof supports automation.

options.title: Fold into terminal-session monitoring
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader saturated-session monitoring work tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91832 and design one shared context-pressure surface.

options.title: Keep reporting-only behavior
options.body: Do not add parent recovery semantics yet; rely on session rows, status, and external monitoring until a stronger product design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Define observe-first context-pressure alerts
recommendation.body: Add a narrow diagnostic/session-health contract that alerts the parent/operator when a child crosses a chosen threshold, with recovery left explicit until live proof supports automation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans diagnostics policy and subagent orchestration semantics, and history shows repeated work by this owner across both surfaces.
